rows: `wf` now takes `check`, `ship`, `ask`, `plan` (verbs) and `app`, `vm`, `secret`, `repo` (nouns). `surface::resolve` turns each into the argv of the command that does the work; the 24 old top-level names still run unchanged and print one stderr line naming their replacement (silenced with `WF_ALIAS_NOTICE=0`, which the black-box harness sets). The global `--app` option is also spelled `--frontend`. Deliberate behaviour changes: the new spellings, the notice, `wf --help` listing eight commands. Cost: n=5 medians of 100 runs, `wf --version` 3.69 ms, `wf verify --help` (old name, through the resolver) 3.73 ms, `wf check --help` 3.59 ms; the binary is 11,153,064 bytes. Checks: `surface` unit tests 11 passed; `cli_surface` black box 9 passed; the full `wf-blackbox` run 958 passed with two load-sensitive tests (`cli_work_run` SIGTERM, `cli_browser_attach` scroll) that pass alone, three times, and on a rerun of their files; clippy `-D warnings` clean. One security finding fixed in the same change: the secret-exposure guard (`scripts/guards/block-secret-exposure.mjs`) and the approve deny list (`libraries/hook-runtime/src/deny.json`) matched only the plural noun, so the singular spelling of the value-revealing subcommands would have bypassed them; both now match an optional trailing `s`, with three new guard tests, and the coverage test checks both spellings. The aliases are removed in a later small PR once `rg "wf (verify|deploy|work|dispatch|secrets|auth|agents)\b"` finds nothing outside the alias table.
